old_title: Dog stops play at Leicestershire as title race heats up: county cricket, day three - live
new_title: Somerset return to summit after dog stops play: county cricket, day three - as it happened
old_text:
Here comes Keaton Jennings swinging his bat. Over at Hove, a match sitting in the corner of the season, which feels weird, but there you go, Surrey have slipped to 47 for three.
Hampshire are all out at last, for 73, a pretty sparkling effort from 165-6, thanks largely to an unbeaten 133 from Jake Lehmann. Three wickets each to Stone, Pennington and Sheat. Notts go again.
Take-no-chances Somerset must be waiting for the Nicholls hundred, just 11 away. James Rew tonked a couple of sixes on his way to 21. The lead over Leicestershire 508.
A super catch by Harry Singh, scooping off the turf at slip to give Stanley his third wicket. Glos 169 all out, Taylor unbeaten on 31. Ott comes the brush and the roller and Will Williams on a hat-trick to warm up in the middle.
And Stanley gets his reward, Dhariwal snapped up at a wide slipby Jimmy - his 66 the highest score of the match and the partnership of 70 the highest double act. Glos 156-9 lead by 234.
A dog has stopped play at Grace Road, photo when we have it. Somerset have powered to a lead of 463, a six powered 67 not out from Henry Nicholls leads the way. I don't want to be too forward, but I think they've got enough.
Lancashire's off-on-off wicketkeeper - sent to Essex on loan - collects fifty, he and Akhter frustrating Yorkshire with an unbroken eighth wicket partnership of 60. Essex 157-7, still 233 behind.
A wave to the Guardian's Will Unwin who rang the five minute bell today at Old Trafford, asked by a unwary steward who didn't know the red rose fury within. Dhariwal and Taylor have now stretched the lead to 215, which feels enough already although conditions are looking easier.
A couple of wickets this morning - Kent's Mahmud in the action again, removing the adhesive Montgomery for 46 (Derby 111-2 lead by an already hefty 192); and Dillon Pennington giving Eddie Jack an unwelcome 22nd birthday present, lbw for 3. Hampshire 278-8 trail impatient Notts by 99.
Today four schools will fight it out in the inaugral Knight-Stokes Cup finals at Lord's, the welcome (if long-overdue) competition open to all state secondaries
11am: Boys' Final: Altrincham Grammar School (Cheshire) v. John Hampden Grammar School (Bucks)
3pm: Girls' Final: Penistone Grammar School (Yorkshire) v. Chelmsford County High School (Essex)
The winners will have their names etched onto a new honours board in the Pavilion's Writing Room. To enter a school for next year see here.
In the vast expanse of OT, people are scattered like lost buttons as JA runs in from the JA end. And now George Balderson resumes from the George Balderson end.
A cheesed off Glamorgan coach Richard Dawson after they were bowled out for 69 and 65:
"I've said to the boys that was an unacceptable performance, in front of our home fans.
"I thought yesterday was the bottom of the hole, and the frustration is repeating the mistakes not only from the first innings but from the last few games. If you want to learn, you've got to be honest with yourself, look in the mirror and work out what you need to do, then work forward rather than burying your head in the sand.
"Sometimes you've got to find a way through a tough period, Warwickshire were disciplined, their seam attack were on the money and they've got a top-class spinner.
"We've got to be honest, front up and go again because we've got another massive challenge next week [against Surrey]. We're not burying our heads in the sand, we can't kid ourselves where we're at."
"Top o' the mornin' to you, Tanya," hello there Tim Maitland.
"My mind has been, not distracted exactly, but scrambled - yes scrambled is the word - by the sight of Rahul Chahar running between umpire and stumps to bowl leggies right hand over the wicket for Surrey at Hove.
"Why it's taken me so long to even notice is not the point, although perhaps it's because the 27 year old's last T20i involvement and his only ODI were both in 2021, thus proving that it's not just England who chew up and spit out spin bowlers long before they've reached maturity.
"Chahar still looks like his torso is heading towards gully as he somehow manages to propel the pill towards the stumps. Now I'll admit that I'm probably more adverse to contortions than most having endured a sacrum that will twist out of position at the mere mention of Chubby Checker (key learning, don't try to train full time with professional footballers after you;ve turned 40), but that delivery isn't just "quirky", as the Sussex commentary team described it. It is in direct contradiction to all of the Laws of Nature!
"Meanwhile, did you notice Ishan Kishan, tried and rejected as a red ball player after just two tests in the Caribbean in 2023, ripping up trees in one of the pinnacles of the long form game in India; the Duleep Trophy? Kishan, captaining East Zone, followed up his 270 at a strike rate of 80.83 in their mammoth first innings with another 80 at 81.63 in the second."
Warwickshire threw a bear-shaped gauntlet on the Championship turf by demolishing Glamorgan in less than two days and taking temporary possession of top spot.
After claiming a first-innings lead of 322 through half centuries from Sam Hain and Ed Barnard, Warwickshire's bowlers spatchcocked Glamorgan for 65, including five noughts. Ed Barnard's five for 13 topped the leaderboard. Glamorgan, who made just 130 runs in the match, fell to their biggest loss since 1936. Warwickshire waved 22 points.
Jake Lehmann's unbeaten 115 kept relegation-flirters Hampshire in it at Trent Bridge. A seventh-wicket stand of 97 with Scott Currie frustrated Notts who had one eye on events at Sophia Gardens.
A second century partnership of the match between Tom Lammonby and Josh Thomas shimmied fellow pennant-chasers Somerset to a dominant position. They had earlier whipped out Leicestershire for 157. Leicestershire's top scorer was Nick Kelly, whose 39 was interrupted when a wasp flew inside his shirt.
At the other end of Division One, Yorkshire's Dom Bess and Kuldeep Yadav bewildered Essex, with three wickets each. They had earlier frustrated in an eighth-wicket stand of 83, Bess undefeated on 80. Essex were further hit when Jamie Porter limped off, though Sam Cook later returned from the Test.
Durham's serene passage back to Division One continued as their big beasts turned on the charm. Brydon Carse whistled through the Middlesex tail to finish with five wickets. Ben McKinney then delighted with his third free-flowing century of the summer.
There were 22 wickets in the frantic basement battle at Old Trafford. After bowling out Gloucestershire for 212, Lancashire were dismissed for 134, something of a triumph from 43 for six, with Will Williams pocketing a career best six for 24 at his former home. George Balderson top scored and then high-kneed through 13 overs on the trot to take four for 23 as Gloucestershire wilted to 118 for eight - but with a crucial lead of 189.
Ben Aitchison passed 50 wickets for the season as Derbyshire dominated against Kent, whose promotion rivals Northamptonshire had a good day against Worcestershire thanks to 110 from Saif Zaib and three evening wickets from Harry Conway.
Good morning! Only ten cricketing dawns left till the end of the season, and who knows how many till our AI masters destroy us all. In the meantime, autumn falls and settles. Warwickshire have points in the bag, can Somerset and Notts push through? Will Kent re-find their mojo, will Northants sneak through on the inside? And who will win the Williams v Balderson nibble-nibble contest at Old Trafford. All this and more from 10.30am, do join us.
new_text:
In a round of staggering collapses, batting sides continued to strap on their roller skates and head to the ice rink. At Grace Road, Leicestershire were rumbled for 145, a 377 run-victory that puts Somerset back on the top of the table, that longed-for first title still in reach.
Somerset set Leicestershire 523 to win after waiting for New Zealand signing Henry Nicholls to reach his first Championship century. Craig Overton (four for 33) and Jack Leach (three for 30) then stormed through Leicestershire's defences. The most entertaining moment for a loyal crowd was when a runaway husky frolicked on the pitch.
At Trent Bridge, defending champions Nottinghamshire were bowled out for 104 by a rampant Hampshire attack. Seventeen-year-old Manny Lumsden, bowling with fire and bounce, sprung out five for 36, including top scorer Joe Clarke for 37. Hampshire, set 178, were soon batting on a see-saw of their own against Olly Stone (three for 15) and Dillon Pennington (three for 18). They had stumbled to 61 for six when bad light brought temporary respite.
At Headingley, Essex fell foul of Kuldeep Yadav, whose six for 50 has almost ensured Yorkshire's Division One spot next season. At one stage Essex were 26 for five following on, but Paul Walter's 48 and George Bell's 28 ensured they passed 100. Kuldeep can tuck career-best match figures of 10 for 120 into his wallet. Sam Cook, who arrived late, unwanted at the Test, didn't bowl a ball.
Northamptonshire took 20 points from their six-wicket victory over Worcestershire, leapfrogging promotion challengers Kent. They had a more difficult day at the County Ground against Derbyshire, who have set the visitors 434 to win after half centuries for Brooke Guest, Luis Reece and the in-form Martin Andersson.
Elsewhere, an unbeaten maiden first-class 50 from Rocky Flintoff gave Lancashire a glimmer of hope for their first win since April. They trail Gloucestershire by 128 runs with four wickets remaining.
Congratulations Yorkshire, Somerset and Northants. Five games left, four improbable run-chases, one could-be and one nailed-on draw. Thanks for your company, we'll be back tomorrow to tidy up this round and see if the weather can prevent Notts rejoining the tight triple-act at the top. Have a lovely evening.
So just two games in play - Hampshire's doomed chase at Trent Bridge (51-6) and the strangely normal game at Hove where Surrey 245-5 meander towards Sussex's 393. Mahipal Lomor 56 not out.
New Road:Northamptonshire 289 and 96-4 BEAT Worcestershire 200 and 182 by seven wickets.
Against the run of play round the counties, Northants stem the flow of a collapse and ease to victory. Zaib a third wicket for Usama just before the close but a comfortable six-wicket win, vital in the promotion scramble, as they edge into second spot behind Durham.
Grace Road:Somerset 363 and 316-5dec BEAT Leicestershire 157 and 145 by 377 runs
Leicestershire's biggest defeat by Somerset. Ben Cox top scored with 39. Overton 4-33; Leach 3-30. Somerset remain five wickets ahead of Warwickshire in the table.
Now Stone has three, Brown shrugs as he traces a wide one and second slip gobbles first slip's catch. Hampshire 27-6 and Notts nearly there which is just as well as Somerset already are...
I think my chances of doing my over by over shift on Saturday have swirled down the sink. Pakistan 0-1 off the first ball of the innings.
And there goes the fourth wicket at Trent Bridge! Jack Lehmann plants his feet, eyes on the short wide prize, but can only edge through to the keeper. Hants 11-4.
Olly Stone sends Hampshire No. 3 Toby Albert on his way, as Hameed at cover dives like a slip cradle and collects just a sneeze from the ground. Hampshire 11-3.
That Hampshire target has turned and is sprinting into the distance, both openers out. One each to Stone (Organ pulling to mid-on) and Pennington (Gubbins nibbling behind). Hampshire 11 for two.
A sixth wicket at OT, Walkden undone by Kishore, gets a thin edge to Bracey. But Flintoff marches on, back foot punch off Kishore racing to the boundary.
Oooof! At Trent Bridge, Olly Stone's first ball explodes at Felix Organ as Hampshire start their chase.
Following-on, Essex were ushered out for 113 in 40 overs. Six wickets for Yadav, who finishes with a career-best first-class match figures of 10 for 120, and Yorkshire are almost safe.
Headingley:Yorkshire 390 BEAT Essex 171 and 113 by 106 runs
With a nudge to the fine leg boundary! A first fifty in first-class cricket, eight fours and an arcing six. Applause from the Lancashire dressing room. Game on?
Lumsden collects his fifth. He is given the ball and Notts usher him ahead to lead the side off. Notts all out 104, Lumsden 5-36. But can Hampshire really make 178? We'll find out after tea.
Here at OT where the rain is surely coming, Rocky Flintoff has 35, his highest first-class score. Kishore, magnificent hair bubbling above his headband, wheels in. Lancs have reduced the target to 154.
Belatedly put on the live stream, Notts 76-7, . There's a lashing wind adding to Notts' woes. Seventeen (17!) year old Manny Lumsden, rapid, bounces Olly Stone. A maiden, two for 25.
Glorious keeping by Bracey. Shetty, for the second ball in a row, takes a huge stride forward to negate the spin of Kishore. Back boot out by an eyelash as he whips off the bails. Lancs 68-5.
Somerset are continuing to chip, hammer, chisel their way through Leicestershire - now 46-4, Shaikh barely looked up after being hit mid pad by Overton.
Who switched the drinks at Trent Bridge? Champs Notts are 54 for six. Only Joe Clarke in double figures. Three for Jack, two for teenage Lumsden, one for Currie. The lead is 127.
With the Manchester skies darkening, Harris plants his front foot and drives, edging to Hammond at third slip for catch number three of the innings. Lancs 55-4.
